### z80 POP IY

PUSH captures the index before either stack access. POP replaces it only after both reads and SP updates. JP (index) copies the index to PC without reading memory. EX (SP),index captures the index, then SP; it reads low/high, writes high/low, and finally replaces the index. Flags and SP are unchanged by EX, and failed accesses retain completed effects without replacing the index.

```text

  low:u8 := source "pop byte through SP" {
    address:u16 := read SP
    byte:u8 := read memory[address]
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := addWrap(pointer, 0001:u16)
    yield byte
  }
  high:u8 := source "pop byte through SP" {
    address:u16 := read SP
    byte:u8 := read memory[address]
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := addWrap(pointer, 0001:u16)
    yield byte
  }
  yield concatHighLow(high, low)
}
write IY:u16 := word
```

### z80 RLC (IX+d)

Only rrr=110 is documented: indexed bit operations act on memory without an extra register copy. `00 ooo 110` selects the seven documented shifts/rotates; ooo=110 (SLL) is excluded. `01/10/11 bbb 110` selects BIT/RES/SET. The same memory actions and masks used on the CB page preserve flag order, unchanged writes, and partial failures here.

```text

base:u16 := read IX
address := addWrap(base, signExtend16(displacement))
perform "RLC memory" {
  address:u16 := address
  original:u8 := read memory[address]
  result := shiftLeft(original, topBit(original))
  flags "Z80 CB rotation and shift flags" simultaneously {
    S := topBit(result)
    Z := isZero(result)
```

```text
  original:u8 := read memory[address]

}
```

### z80 write the next instruction address

Reset sets PC, I, R, and IM to zero, disables both interrupt flip-flops, clears both deferral latches, and releases HALT. It preserves both register banks, IX, IY, SP, and RAM. Reset records detached before/after snapshots and an empty access list: it neither reads a vector nor fabricates a power-on state. `CpuZ80ResetRecord` has no instruction or step outcome. Repeated reset has the same defined effects and produces fresh records. Preserving registers whose reset values the manual leaves unspecified is a deterministic model policy, not a claim about physical power-on values. An example's fresh factory instead restores its initial CPU, program, and RAM.

```text
word:u16 := input
write PC:u16 := word
```

### z80 advance the low seven refresh bits

Operands are then read through the live PC, advancing it after each successful read. All addresses wrap to sixteen bits; words read low byte first. An access failure retains earlier effects, including committed PC/R, but does not retire the instruction. Each step executes one instruction or one repeating block iteration and records ordered memory and port accesses.

```text
count:u8 := input
original:u8 := read R
write R:u8 := bitOr(bitAnd(original, 80:u8), bitAnd(addWrap(original, count), 7F:u8))
```

### z80 consume NMI inhibition

Operands are then read through the live PC, advancing it after each successful read. All addresses wrap to sixteen bits; words read low byte first. An access failure retains earlier effects, including committed PC/R, but does not retire the instruction. Each step executes one instruction or one repeating block iteration and records ordered memory and port accesses.


### z80 replace packed F

F packs `S Z 0 H 0 PV N C`, reading the six flags in that order. PUSH AF captures A before this view; POP AF writes A before replacing the flags object. The status action below supplies that replacement to the existing stack body. All six new flag values are computed before the old object is replaced.

```text
status:u8 := input
replace flags "restore all documented flags" simultaneously {
  S := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 80:u8)))
  Z := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 40:u8)))
  H := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 10:u8)))
  PV := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 04:u8)))
  N := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 02:u8)))
  C := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 01:u8)))
} // Replace the complete flag object.
```

Flags preserved throughout: none.

Capture A without reading incoming flags. Apply the table's flags before writing the byte result to A. A failed operand read prevents every action effect.

```text
  Z := isZero(result)
  H := halfCarry4(left, right)
  PV := addOverflow(left, right)
  N := 0:flag
  C := carry(left, right)
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
write A:u8 := result
```

### z80 push return PC then jump

CALL captures its complete target before the condition. On a taken path it captures the return PC, pushes both bytes, then changes PC. RST uses `11 ttt 111` to call one of eight fixed addresses in the first 64 bytes. The shared action ensures both retain completed stack effects on failure, with PC replaced only after both writes succeed.

```text
returnPC:u16 := read PC
perform "push a captured word" {
  word:u16 := returnPC
  perform "push a captured byte" {
    byte:u8 := highByte(word)
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0001:u16)
    address:u16 := read SP
    write memory[address] := byte
  }
  perform "push a captured byte" {
    byte:u8 := lowByte(word)
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0001:u16)
    address:u16 := read SP
    write memory[address] := byte
  }
}
write PC:u16 := target
```

### z80 push PC before selecting and reading the IRQ vector

After acknowledgement, IM selects a supplied instruction or a vector entry. Mode 1 ignores the byte and calls `$0038`. Mode 2 pushes PC before forming the vector address from current I and the supplied byte; then it reads the target low byte first. This preserves stack/vector overlap and each partial failure. The low vector byte may be odd, and its following address wraps at sixteen bits.

```text

returnPC:u16 := read PC
perform "push a captured word" {
  word:u16 := returnPC
  perform "push a captured byte" {
    byte:u8 := highByte(word)
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0001:u16)
    address:u16 := read SP
    write memory[address] := byte
  }
  perform "push a captured byte" {
    byte:u8 := lowByte(word)
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0001:u16)
    address:u16 := read SP
    write memory[address] := byte
  }
}
modeOne:flag := test control im equals 1
when modeOne {
  write PC:u16 := 0038:u16
}
when not(modeOne) {
  high:u8 := read I
  address := concatHighLow(high, byte)
  low:u8 := read memory[address]
  highTarget:u8 := read memory[addWrap(address, 0001:u16)]
  write PC:u16 := concatHighLow(highTarget, low)
}
```

### z80 rewind current PC for another block iteration

Each step performs one iteration. Repeating forms rewind current PC by two while another iteration is required, so the next step refetches both opcode bytes and exposes an interrupt boundary. BC starts as a sixteen-bit count; zero wraps to $FFFF on the first iteration. Direction is a wrapped word delta. The single/repeat sources bind encoding choices without accessing state.

```text

parity:flag := read PV
flags "repeat parity correction" simultaneously {
  PV := not(xor(parity, evenParity8(bitAnd(operand, 07:u8))))
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
```

```text
    perform "correct parity between block I/O iterations" {
      operand:u8 := adjusted
      parity:flag := read PV
      flags "repeat parity correction" simultaneously {
        PV := not(xor(parity, evenParity8(bitAnd(operand, 07:u8))))
      } // Preserve unlisted flags.
    }
  }
  when not(carry) {
    perform "correct parity between block I/O iterations" {
      operand:u8 := repeatCounter
      parity:flag := read PV
      flags "repeat parity correction" simultaneously {
        PV := not(xor(parity, evenParity8(bitAnd(operand, 07:u8))))
      } // Preserve unlisted flags.
    }
```

### 8088 write AL, preserving its other half

Each read captures its stored word once. A write captures the **live** word again at writeback, preserving its other half even if a fetch or flag update has changed that word since the earlier operand read. Actions own their local captures, so several byte writes can occur in one instruction without sharing temporary values. Native instruction definitions use these same chapter views and actions while their bodies await migration.

```text
byte:u8 := input
preservedWord:u16 := read AX
write AX:u16 := concatHighLow(highByte(preservedWord), byte)
```

### 8088 replace all FLAGS

The low byte is `SF ZF 0 AF 0 PF 1 CF`. The full original-chip FLAGS word adds TF/IF/DF/OF in bits 8–11 and sets bits 12–15. Packing reads CF/PF/AF/ZF/SF, then TF/IF/DF/OF for the word. Reserved bits are ignored on restoration. SAHF updates five fields of the existing flags object. Full restoration replaces all nine fields, and is shared by POPF and IRET. Their interrupt-deferral and stack rules remain with those instructions.

```text
status:u16 := input
replace flags "restore FLAGS" simultaneously {
  CF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0001:u16)))
  PF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0004:u16)))
  AF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0010:u16)))
  ZF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0040:u16)))
  SF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0080:u16)))
  TF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0100:u16)))
  IF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0200:u16)))
  DF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0400:u16)))
  OF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0800:u16)))
} // Replace the complete flag object.
```

Flags preserved throughout: none.

### 8088 write a captured 8-bit memory operand

`projectAddress(segment, offset, 4, 20)` expresses the physical projection: shift the word segment by four, add the word offset, and keep twenty bits. Word transfers read/write the low byte first. Each uses the captured pointer for both bytes, regardless of changes during a memory callback.

```text
pointer:u32 := input
contents:u8 := input
segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
offset := low16(pointer)
write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)] := contents
```

### 8088 write a resolved 8-bit operand

The operand helpers interpret `11 xxx rrr` as a register and every other mode as the already captured pointer. They never resolve the address again.     perform "write DL, preserving its other half" {

```text
      preservedWord:u16 := read DX
      write DX:u16 := concatHighLow(highByte(preservedWord), byte)

  }
  case (byte & C7) = C3 {
    perform "write BL, preserving its other half" {
      byte:u8 := contents
      preservedWord:u16 := read BX
      write BX:u16 := concatHighLow(highByte(preservedWord), byte)
    }
  }
  case (byte & C7) = C4 {
    perform "write AH, preserving its other half" {
      byte:u8 := contents
      preservedWord:u16 := read AX
      write AX:u16 := concatHighLow(byte, lowByte(preservedWord))
    }
  }
  case (byte & C7) = C5 {
    perform "write CH, preserving its other half" {
      byte:u8 := contents
      preservedWord:u16 := read CX
      write CX:u16 := concatHighLow(byte, lowByte(preservedWord))
    }
  }
  case (byte & C7) = C6 {
    perform "write DH, preserving its other half" {
      byte:u8 := contents
      preservedWord:u16 := read DX
      write DX:u16 := concatHighLow(byte, lowByte(preservedWord))
    }
  }

  case (byte & 80) = 00 {

      pointer:u32 := pointer
```

### 8088 restore stacked FLAGS with recognition delay

PUSHF (`1001 1100`) captures the packed FLAGS word before pushing. POPF (`1001 1101`) reads the complete word before consulting live IF. A transition from clear IF to set IF requests INTR deferral before replacing the flag object. Reserved bits are ignored by the chapter's existing restore policy. IRET uses this same chapter action after completing its far return.

```text

  segment:u16 := read SS
  offset:u16 := read SP
  word:u16 := source "read a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
    pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
    segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
    offset := low16(pointer)
    low:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)]
    high:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)]
    yield concatHighLow(high, low)
  }
  pointer:u16 := read SP
  write SP:u16 := addWrap(pointer, 0002:u16)
  yield word
}
oldIF:flag := read IF
when not(oldIF) {
  when not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0200:u16))) {
    request INTR deferral at successful retirement
  }
}
perform "replace all FLAGS" {
  status:u16 := status
  replace flags "restore FLAGS" simultaneously {
    CF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0001:u16)))
    PF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0004:u16)))
    AF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0010:u16)))
    ZF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0040:u16)))
    SF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0080:u16)))
    TF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0100:u16)))
    IF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0200:u16)))
    DF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0400:u16)))
    OF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0800:u16)))
  } // Replace the complete flag object.
}
```

```text
    yield concatHighLow(high, low)
  }
  pointer:u16 := read SP
  write SP:u16 := addWrap(pointer, 0002:u16)
  yield word
}
```

### 8088 advance live indices and decide repetition

After data and comparison flags, read live DF to select the signed byte/word stride. Advance live SI before DI when both apply. Repeated forms then decrement live CX and reread it; only a nonzero count tests the new ZF for CMPS/SCAS. A continuing operation rewinds IP to the supplied prefix start. The next step refetches prefixes, so code changes, snapshot resumption, and interrupt offers remain observable. The finishing action's numeric selectors describe which indices and repeat condition the calling family uses.

```text

useSI:u8 := input
useDI:u8 := input
compares:u8 := input
repeatMode:u8 := input
startIP:u16 := input

size := addWrap(zeroExtend16(width), 0001:u16)
delta := select(backward, subtract(0000:u16, size), size)
when not(isZero(useSI)) {
  position:u16 := read SI
  write SI:u16 := addWrap(position, delta)
}
when not(isZero(useDI)) {
  position:u16 := read DI
  write DI:u16 := addWrap(position, delta)
}
when not(isZero(repeatMode)) {
  count:u16 := read CX
  write CX:u16 := subtract(count, 0001:u16)
  remaining:u16 := read CX
  when not(isZero(remaining)) {
    when isZero(compares) {
      write IP:u16 := startIP
    }
    when not(isZero(compares)) {
      equal:flag := read ZF
      when xor(equal, isZero(bitXor(repeatMode, 02:u8))) {
        write IP:u16 := startIP
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### 8088 sample TEST for initial WAIT or continuation

Missing/malformed TEST callbacks and thrown device errors propagate without a record. TEST must return a Boolean without coercion. Initial instruction fetches remain reflected in IP; a failed continuation leaves its waiting state and IP unchanged. No recognition latch changes until the sample succeeds. If an ESC operand read fails, no external request is issued. If the ESC callback fails, completed reads, fetched IP, and device effects remain; no rollback is attempted. Callbacks preserve their receiver and may inspect snapshots but cannot reenter `step`, `reset`, or `interrupt`. Reset clears waiting and recognition state while preserving connections and devices; it neither samples TEST nor issues ESC.

```text
resuming:u8 := input
high:flag := sample and record physical TEST level; high waits, low releases
write waiting:boolean := high
when isZero(resuming) {
  when high {
    position:u16 := read IP
    write IP:u16 := subtract(position, 0001:u16)
  }
}
when not(isZero(resuming)) {
  when not(high) {
    position:u16 := read IP
    write IP:u16 := addWrap(position, 0001:u16)
  }
}
when not(high) {
  request all interrupt deferral at successful retirement
}
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 capture dummy word before ESC delivery

ESC uses `1101 1 ooo` and ModR/M `mm ppp rrr`; `ooo:ppp` forms the six-bit coprocessor opcode. Register forms send the selector without reading CPU registers. Memory forms resolve the ordinary segmented address and read a complete dummy word even if no coprocessor is connected. Only then do they send the captured segment, offset, physical address, and word. The device adapter detaches requests and records only successful delivery. ESC itself leaves CPU state and flags unchanged; no coprocessor arithmetic is emulated.

```text
opcode:u8 := input
postbyte:u8 := input
pointer:u32 := input
segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
offset := low16(pointer)
contents:u16 := source "read a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
  pointer:u32 := pointer
  segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
  offset := low16(pointer)
  low:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)]
  high:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)]
  yield concatHighLow(high, low)
}
send and record ESC opcode opcode, ModR/M postbyte, captured memory segment:offset at projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits) with word contents; device receives a detached request; record only after callback success
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 reset control state, preserving general registers and RAM

Reset selects CS:IP=`FFFF:0000`, clears DS/SS/ES, all nine flags, halt/wait, and the three recognition latches. It reads no vector: physical `$FFFF0` is the next instruction address. General registers and RAM are preserved because Intel leaves those register reset values unspecified. This is a deterministic model policy, not a claim about their power-on values.

```text

write IP:u16 := 0000:u16
write waiting:boolean := false
write halted:boolean := false
write trapPending:boolean := false
write recognitionDeferred:boolean := false
write interruptDeferred:boolean := false
write ES:u16 := 0000:u16
write SS:u16 := 0000:u16
write DS:u16 := 0000:u16
replace flags "clear every modeled flag" simultaneously {
  CF := 0:flag
  PF := 0:flag
  AF := 0:flag
  ZF := 0:flag
  SF := 0:flag
  TF := 0:flag
  IF := 0:flag
  DF := 0:flag
  OF := 0:flag
} // Replace the complete flag object.
```

### 8088 release WAIT and HLT before acknowledgement or entry

Unsupported encodings restore the original IP and skip retirement; failed host callbacks retain completed effects and propagate without a record. A divide error enters type 0 from the **following** IP, as on the original 8088, then retires with the original trap sample. Software entry reports its own vector after its explicit effects. Neither kind cancels an owed trap. External INTR/NMI offers share the same reentrancy guard. Their ordered gates below preserve deferral-before-masking and reject without acknowledgement or wake-up. Eligible INTR validates callback presence before releasing WAIT/HLT, then obtains its vector. Both sources use the chapter's shared entry action.

```text
write waiting:boolean := false
write halted:boolean := false
```

### 8088 ADD AL,n

Do not read incoming flags. Set CF/AF/OF, then ZF/SF/PF from the wrapped result. Write AL/AX after flags and preserve TF/IF/DF.

```text

  byte:u8 := fetch byte
  yield byte
}
left:u8 := source "low byte of AX" {
  word:u16 := read AX
  yield lowByte(word)
}
result := addWrap(left, right)
flags "8088 ADD flags" simultaneously {
  CF := carry(left, right, 0:flag)
  AF := halfCarry4(left, right, 0:flag)
  OF := addOverflow(left, right, 0:flag)
  ZF := isZero(result)
  SF := topBit(result)
  PF := evenParity8(result)
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
perform "write AL, preserving its other half" {
  byte:u8 := result
  preservedWord:u16 := read AX
  write AX:u16 := concatHighLow(highByte(preservedWord), byte)
}
```

### 8088 PUSH ES

Segment PUSH/POP uses `000 ss 11 p`, with `ss=00/01/10/11` selecting ES/CS/SS/DS. POP CS is undocumented. After any documented segment pop, request inhibition of **all** interrupt recognition at successful retirement. The request does not immediately change a stored boundary latch; a later failure leaves it uncommitted. The same rule applies to MOV into a segment.

```text
original:u16 := read ES
perform "push a captured word" {
  word:u16 := original
  pointer:u16 := read SP
  write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0002:u16)
  segment:u16 := read SS
  offset:u16 := read SP
  perform "write a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
    pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
    contents:u16 := word
    segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
    offset := low16(pointer)
    write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)] := lowByte(contents)
    write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)] := highByte(contents)
  }
}
```

### 8088 DAA

AAA/AAS adjust unpacked AL and AH independently, then mask AL to its low nibble. A carry/borrow from AL's byte adjustment does not adjust AH a second time. AF/CF report adjustment; undefined OF/SF/ZF/PF are preserved. AAM splits AL into decimal quotient AH and remainder AL; AAD combines AH×10+AL into AL modulo 256 and clears AH. Only the documented fixed second byte `0A` is supported. AAM/AAD set SF/ZF/PF from AL and preserve undefined CF/AF/OF. CBW and CWD sign-extend the accumulator without changing flags.

```text
original:u8 := source "low byte of AX" {
  word:u16 := read AX
  yield lowByte(word)
}
low:u8 := source "low digit needs correction" {
  original:u8 := original
  decision:u8 := match byte select(not(borrow(bitAnd(original, 0F:u8), 0A:u8)), 01:u8, 00:u8) {
    case (byte & FF) = 01 {
      yield 01:u8
    }
    case (byte & FF) = 00 {
      incoming:flag := read AF
      yield select(incoming, 01:u8, 00:u8)
    }
    otherwise return outcome "unsupported"; no later effects
  }
  yield decision
}
high:u8 := source "high digit needs correction" {
  original:u8 := original
  auxiliary:flag := read AF
  decision:u8 := match byte select(not(borrow(original, select(auxiliary, A0:u8, 9A:u8))), 01:u8, 00:u8) {
    case (byte & FF) = 01 {
      yield 01:u8
    }
    case (byte & FF) = 00 {
      incoming:flag := read CF
      yield select(incoming, 01:u8, 00:u8)
    }
    otherwise return outcome "unsupported"; no later effects
  }
  yield decision
}
result := addWrap(original, addWrap(select(isZero(low), 00:u8, 06:u8), select(isZero(high), 00:u8, 60:u8)))
flags "packed decimal correction" simultaneously {
  AF := not(isZero(low))
  CF := not(isZero(high))
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
perform "write AL, preserving its other half" {
  byte:u8 := result
  preservedWord:u16 := read AX
  write AX:u16 := concatHighLow(highByte(preservedWord), byte)
}
flags "zero, sign, and parity" simultaneously {
  ZF := isZero(result)
  SF := topBit(result)
  PF := evenParity8(result)
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
```

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 DAS

AAA/AAS adjust unpacked AL and AH independently, then mask AL to its low nibble. A carry/borrow from AL's byte adjustment does not adjust AH a second time. AF/CF report adjustment; undefined OF/SF/ZF/PF are preserved. AAM splits AL into decimal quotient AH and remainder AL; AAD combines AH×10+AL into AL modulo 256 and clears AH. Only the documented fixed second byte `0A` is supported. AAM/AAD set SF/ZF/PF from AL and preserve undefined CF/AF/OF. CBW and CWD sign-extend the accumulator without changing flags.

```text
  word:u16 := read AX
  yield lowByte(word)
}
low:u8 := source "low digit needs correction" {
  original:u8 := original
  decision:u8 := match byte select(not(borrow(bitAnd(original, 0F:u8), 0A:u8)), 01:u8, 00:u8) {
    case (byte & FF) = 01 {
      yield 01:u8
    }
    case (byte & FF) = 00 {
      incoming:flag := read AF
      yield select(incoming, 01:u8, 00:u8)
    }
    otherwise return outcome "unsupported"; no later effects
  }
  yield decision
}

  original:u8 := original
  auxiliary:flag := read AF

    case (byte & FF) = 01 {
      yield 01:u8
    }
    case (byte & FF) = 00 {
      incoming:flag := read CF
      yield select(incoming, 01:u8, 00:u8)
    }
    otherwise return outcome "unsupported"; no later effects
  }
  yield decision
}

  AF := not(isZero(low))
  CF := not(isZero(high))
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
perform "write AL, preserving its other half" {
  byte:u8 := result
  preservedWord:u16 := read AX
  write AX:u16 := concatHighLow(highByte(preservedWord), byte)
}
flags "zero, sign, and parity" simultaneously {
  ZF := isZero(result)
  SF := topBit(result)
  PF := evenParity8(result)
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
```

### 8088 INC AX

`0100 d rrr` selects INC (`d=0`) or DEC (`d=1`) of a word register. Capture the register, then CF. Add or subtract one with sixteen-bit wrapping, update arithmetic flags, restore captured CF, and only then write the register. Preserve TF/IF/DF. This deliberately retains the model's flag-write ordering, including its transient CF update if a host observer interrupts execution.

```text

preservedCarry:flag := read CF
right := 0001:u16
result := addWrap(left, right)
flags "8088 ADD flags" simultaneously {
  CF := carry(left, right, 0:flag)
  AF := halfCarry4(left, right, 0:flag)
  OF := addOverflow(left, right, 0:flag)
  ZF := isZero(result)
  SF := topBit(result)
  PF := evenParity8(lowByte(result))
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
flags "restore captured carry" simultaneously {
  CF := preservedCarry
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
write AX:u16 := result
```

### 8088 PUSH AX

`0101 p rrr` selects register PUSH/POP. Original 8088 PUSH SP differs from other registers: its source is the captured SP minus two, before the stack's independent pointer update. The separate source makes that exception visible; all other encoded registers use the ordinary register catalogue.

```text
original:u16 := read AX
perform "push a captured word" {
  word:u16 := original
  pointer:u16 := read SP
  write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0002:u16)
  segment:u16 := read SS
  offset:u16 := read SP
```

### 8088 JO rel8

Compound conditions short-circuit: JBE/JA read CF before ZF, and JLE/JG read ZF before SF and OF. The numeric source returns zero or one so the polarity bit can invert a captured decision without rereading any flag.

```text
offset:u8 := source "immediate byte" {
  byte:u8 := fetch byte
  yield byte
}
condition:u8 := source "JO" {
  yield 00:u8
}
decision:u8 := source "ordered branch test" {
  condition:u8 := condition
  positive:u8 := match byte shiftBitsRight(condition, 1) {
    case (byte & FF) = 00 {
      test:flag := read OF
      yield select(test, 01:u8, 00:u8)
    }
    case (byte & FF) = 01 {
      test:flag := read CF
      yield select(test, 01:u8, 00:u8)
    }
    case (byte & FF) = 02 {
      test:flag := read ZF
      yield select(test, 01:u8, 00:u8)
    }
    case (byte & FF) = 03 {
      first:flag := read CF
      result:u8 := match byte select(first, 01:u8, 00:u8) {
        case (byte & FF) = 01 {
          yield 01:u8
        }
        case (byte & FF) = 00 {
          second:flag := read ZF
          yield select(second, 01:u8, 00:u8)
        }
        otherwise return outcome "unsupported"; no later effects
      }
      yield result
    }
    case (byte & FF) = 04 {
      test:flag := read SF
      yield select(test, 01:u8, 00:u8)
    }
    case (byte & FF) = 05 {
      test:flag := read PF
      yield select(test, 01:u8, 00:u8)
    }
    case (byte & FF) = 06 {
      sign:flag := read SF
      overflow:flag := read OF
      yield select(xor(sign, overflow), 01:u8, 00:u8)
    }
    case (byte & FF) = 07 {
      first:flag := read ZF
      result:u8 := match byte select(first, 01:u8, 00:u8) {
        case (byte & FF) = 01 {
          yield 01:u8
        }
        case (byte & FF) = 00 {
          sign:flag := read SF
          overflow:flag := read OF
          yield select(xor(sign, overflow), 01:u8, 00:u8)
        }
        otherwise return outcome "unsupported"; no later effects
      }
      yield result
    }
    otherwise return outcome "unsupported"; no later effects
  }
  yield bitXor(positive, bitAnd(condition, 01:u8))
}
when not(isZero(decision)) {
  perform "branch from live post-fetch IP" {
    offset:u16 := signExtend16(offset)
    position:u16 := read IP
    write IP:u16 := addWrap(position, offset)
  }
}
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 NOP

`1001 0 rrr` exchanges AX with the selected word register: capture that register before AX, write AX, then write the selected register. The documented NOP encoding `$90` retains the same self-exchange schedule, including both reads and writes; no flags or memory are touched.

```text
selected:u16 := read AX
accumulator:u16 := read AX
write AX:u16 := selected
write AX:u16 := accumulator
```

### 8088 CBW

AAM/AAD (`1101 010 d`) require the documented `$0A` radix before accessing AX. AAM splits AL into quotient and remainder; AAD combines AH × 10 + AL and clears AH. After writing AX, both reread AL for ZF/SF/PF. CBW and CWD (`1001 100 s`) extend AL's sign to AX or AX's sign to DX without flag effects.

```text
word:u16 := read AX
write AX:u16 := signExtend16(lowByte(word))
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

After writing AX, both reread AL for ZF/SF/PF. CBW and CWD (`1001 100 s`) extend AL's sign to AX or AX's sign to DX without flag effects.

```text
word:u16 := read AX
write DX:u16 := select(topBit(word), FFFF:u16, 0000:u16)
```

### 8088 CALL ptr16:16

Near relative CALL (`1110 1000`) fetches its displacement, captures and pushes return IP, then adds the displacement to **live IP after both writes**. Immediate far CALL (`1001 1010`) fetches the complete offset and segment before pushing CS and then live IP. Far JMP (`1110 1010`) fetches the same pointer and writes CS before IP without a stack access. The far-transfer action also serves the indirect FF forms, after they have read their complete memory pointer.

```text
targetOffset:u16 := source "immediate word, low byte first" {
  low:u8 := fetch byte
  high:u8 := fetch byte
  yield concatHighLow(high, low)
}
targetSegment:u16 := source "immediate word, low byte first" {
  low:u8 := fetch byte
  high:u8 := fetch byte
  yield concatHighLow(high, low)
}
perform "save live CS:IP then commit the target" {
  targetOffset:u16 := targetOffset
  targetSegment:u16 := targetSegment
  returnCS:u16 := read CS
  perform "push a captured word" {
    word:u16 := returnCS
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0002:u16)
    segment:u16 := read SS
    offset:u16 := read SP
    perform "write a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
      pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
      contents:u16 := word
      segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
      offset := low16(pointer)
      write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)] := lowByte(contents)
      write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)] := highByte(contents)
    }
  }
  returnIP:u16 := read IP
  perform "push a captured word" {
    word:u16 := returnIP
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0002:u16)
    segment:u16 := read SS
    offset:u16 := read SP
    perform "write a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
      pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
      contents:u16 := word
      segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
      offset := low16(pointer)
      write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)] := lowByte(contents)
      write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)] := highByte(contents)
    }
  }
  perform "commit captured CS:IP" {
    targetOffset:u16 := targetOffset
    targetSegment:u16 := targetSegment
    write CS:u16 := targetSegment
    write IP:u16 := targetOffset
  }
}
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 WAIT

Missing/malformed TEST callbacks and thrown device errors propagate without a record. TEST must return a Boolean without coercion. Initial instruction fetches remain reflected in IP; a failed continuation leaves its waiting state and IP unchanged. No recognition latch changes until the sample succeeds. If an ESC operand read fails, no external request is issued. If the ESC callback fails, completed reads, fetched IP, and device effects remain; no rollback is attempted. Callbacks preserve their receiver and may inspect snapshots but cannot reenter `step`, `reset`, or `interrupt`. Reset clears waiting and recognition state while preserving connections and devices; it neither samples TEST nor issues ESC.

```text
perform "sample TEST for initial WAIT or continuation" {
  resuming:u8 := 00:u8
  high:flag := sample and record physical TEST level; high waits, low releases
  write waiting:boolean := high
  when isZero(resuming) {
    when high {
      position:u16 := read IP
      write IP:u16 := subtract(position, 0001:u16)
    }
  }
  when not(isZero(resuming)) {
    when not(high) {
      position:u16 := read IP
      write IP:u16 := addWrap(position, 0001:u16)
    }
  }
  when not(high) {
    request all interrupt deferral at successful retirement
  }
}
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 PUSHF

PUSHF (`1001 1100`) captures the packed FLAGS word before pushing. POPF (`1001 1101`) reads the complete word before consulting live IF. A transition from clear IF to set IF requests INTR deferral before replacing the flag object. Reserved bits are ignored by the chapter's existing restore policy. IRET uses this same chapter action after completing its far return.

```text
original:u16 := source "packed FLAGS word" {
  cf:flag := read CF
  pf:flag := read PF
  af:flag := read AF
  zf:flag := read ZF
  sf:flag := read SF
  tf:flag := read TF
  if:flag := read IF
  df:flag := read DF
  of:flag := read OF
  cfBit := select(cf, 0001:u16, 0000:u16)
  pfBit := select(pf, 0004:u16, 0000:u16)
  afBit := select(af, 0010:u16, 0000:u16)
  zfBit := select(zf, 0040:u16, 0000:u16)
  sfBit := select(sf, 0080:u16, 0000:u16)
  tfBit := select(tf, 0100:u16, 0000:u16)
  ifBit := select(if, 0200:u16, 0000:u16)
  dfBit := select(df, 0400:u16, 0000:u16)
  ofBit := select(of, 0800:u16, 0000:u16)
  arithmetic := bitOr(cfBit, bitOr(pfBit, bitOr(afBit, bitOr(zfBit, sfBit))))
  controls := bitOr(tfBit, bitOr(ifBit, bitOr(dfBit, ofBit)))
  yield bitOr(F002:u16, bitOr(arithmetic, controls))
}
perform "push a captured word" {
  word:u16 := original
  pointer:u16 := read SP
  write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0002:u16)
  segment:u16 := read SS
  offset:u16 := read SP
  perform "write a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
    pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
    contents:u16 := word
    segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
    offset := low16(pointer)
    write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)] := lowByte(contents)
    write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)] := highByte(contents)
  }
}
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 POPF

PUSHF (`1001 1100`) captures the packed FLAGS word before pushing. POPF (`1001 1101`) reads the complete word before consulting live IF. A transition from clear IF to set IF requests INTR deferral before replacing the flag object. Reserved bits are ignored by the chapter's existing restore policy. IRET uses this same chapter action after completing its far return.

```text
perform "restore stacked FLAGS with recognition delay" {
  status:u16 := source "pop segmented word" {
    segment:u16 := read SS
    offset:u16 := read SP
    word:u16 := source "read a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
      pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
      segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
      offset := low16(pointer)
      low:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)]
      high:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)]
      yield concatHighLow(high, low)
    }
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := addWrap(pointer, 0002:u16)
    yield word
  }
  oldIF:flag := read IF
  when not(oldIF) {
    when not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0200:u16))) {
      request INTR deferral at successful retirement
    }
  }
  perform "replace all FLAGS" {
    status:u16 := status
    replace flags "restore FLAGS" simultaneously {
      CF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0001:u16)))
      PF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0004:u16)))
      AF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0010:u16)))
      ZF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0040:u16)))
      SF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0080:u16)))
      TF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0100:u16)))
      IF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0200:u16)))
      DF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0400:u16)))
      OF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0800:u16)))
    } // Replace the complete flag object.
  }
}
```

Flags preserved throughout: none.

### 8088 SAHF

`1001 111d` selects SAHF (`d=0`) or LAHF (`d=1`). SAHF captures AH before updating CF/PF/AF/ZF/SF in layout order; OF/TF/IF/DF and all registers survive. LAHF packs the low flags before writing AH, preserving live AL at writeback and leaving all flags unchanged.

```text
status:u8 := source "high byte of AX" {
  word:u16 := read AX
  yield highByte(word)
}
flags "restore LOWFLAGS" simultaneously {
  CF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 01:u8)))
  PF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 04:u8)))
  AF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 10:u8)))
  ZF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 40:u8)))
  SF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 80:u8)))
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
```

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 LAHF

`1001 111d` selects SAHF (`d=0`) or LAHF (`d=1`). SAHF captures AH before updating CF/PF/AF/ZF/SF in layout order; OF/TF/IF/DF and all registers survive. LAHF packs the low flags before writing AH, preserving live AL at writeback and leaving all flags unchanged.

```text
status:u8 := source "packed low FLAGS" {
  cf:flag := read CF
  pf:flag := read PF
  af:flag := read AF
  zf:flag := read ZF
  sf:flag := read SF
  cfBit := select(cf, 01:u8, 00:u8)
  pfBit := select(pf, 04:u8, 00:u8)
  afBit := select(af, 10:u8, 00:u8)
  zfBit := select(zf, 40:u8, 00:u8)
  sfBit := select(sf, 80:u8, 00:u8)
  yield bitOr(bitOr(bitOr(bitOr(bitOr(02:u8, cfBit), pfBit), afBit), zfBit), sfBit)
}
perform "write AH, preserving its other half" {
  byte:u8 := status
  preservedWord:u16 := read AX
  write AX:u16 := concatHighLow(byte, lowByte(preservedWord))
}
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 TEST AL,n

Do not read incoming flags. Clear OF/CF/AF, then set ZF/SF/PF. Preserve AL/AX and TF/IF/DF.

```text
right:u8 := source "immediate byte" {

  yield byte
}
left:u8 := source "low byte of AX" {
  word:u16 := read AX
  yield lowByte(word)
}
result := bitAnd(left, right)
flags "8088 logical flags" simultaneously {
  OF := 0:flag
  CF := 0:flag
  AF := 0:flag
  ZF := isZero(result)
  SF := topBit(result)
  PF := evenParity8(result)
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
```

### 8088 MOV AL,n

`1011 w rrr` selects MOV: `w=0` takes one immediate byte, `w=1` a low-first word. Fetch the complete immediate before writing the destination. Byte writes retain the current other half of the stored word. Preserve every flag; a failed fetch leaves the destination untouched, while completed fetches and IP advances remain.

```text

  byte:u8 := fetch byte
  yield byte
}
perform "write AL, preserving its other half" {
  byte:u8 := result
  preservedWord:u16 := read AX
  write AX:u16 := concatHighLow(highByte(preservedWord), byte)
}
```

### 8088 RET n

`1100 f 01 n` selects returns: `f=0/1` means near/far, and `n=0` fetches an unsigned discard count while `n=1` discards zero. Fetch that count before any stack read. Pop IP and optional CS before committing either target; then read and adjust live SP, including when the discard count is zero. A failed later read leaves completed pops intact. IRET reuses the far-return action before its separate FLAGS pop, retaining the two commit points.

```text
discard:u16 := source "immediate word, low byte first" {
  low:u8 := fetch byte
  high:u8 := fetch byte
  yield concatHighLow(high, low)
}
perform "return within CS" {
  discard:u16 := discard
  targetIP:u16 := source "pop segmented word" {
    segment:u16 := read SS
    offset:u16 := read SP
    word:u16 := source "read a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
      pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
      segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
      offset := low16(pointer)
      low:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)]
      high:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)]
      yield concatHighLow(high, low)
    }
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := addWrap(pointer, 0002:u16)
    yield word
  }
  write IP:u16 := targetIP
  pointer:u16 := read SP
  write SP:u16 := addWrap(pointer, discard)
}
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 INT3

The formal entry action clears TF then IF and the recognition/wait/halt latches. It pushes FLAGS, live CS, and live IP, then commits target CS and IP after the complete frame succeeds. Software forms use `1100 11 tt`: INT3 (`tt=00`), INT with a fetched type byte (`01`), INTO (`10`), and IRET (`11`). `report interrupt` records completed software delivery; it performs no vector or stack effects itself.

```text
perform "interrupt entry" {
  vector:u8 := 03:u8
  offset := shiftBitsLeft(zeroExtend16(vector), 2)
  targetIP:u16 := source "read a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
    pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(0000:u16, offset)
    segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
    offset := low16(pointer)
    low:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)]
    high:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)]
    yield concatHighLow(high, low)
  }
  targetCS:u16 := source "read a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
    pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(0000:u16, addWrap(offset, 0002:u16))
    segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
    offset := low16(pointer)
    low:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)]
    high:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)]
    yield concatHighLow(high, low)
  }
  savedFlags:u16 := source "packed FLAGS word" {
    cf:flag := read CF
    pf:flag := read PF
    af:flag := read AF
    zf:flag := read ZF
    sf:flag := read SF
    tf:flag := read TF
    if:flag := read IF
    df:flag := read DF
    of:flag := read OF
    cfBit := select(cf, 0001:u16, 0000:u16)
    pfBit := select(pf, 0004:u16, 0000:u16)
    afBit := select(af, 0010:u16, 0000:u16)
    zfBit := select(zf, 0040:u16, 0000:u16)
    sfBit := select(sf, 0080:u16, 0000:u16)
    tfBit := select(tf, 0100:u16, 0000:u16)
    ifBit := select(if, 0200:u16, 0000:u16)
    dfBit := select(df, 0400:u16, 0000:u16)
    ofBit := select(of, 0800:u16, 0000:u16)
    arithmetic := bitOr(cfBit, bitOr(pfBit, bitOr(afBit, bitOr(zfBit, sfBit))))
    controls := bitOr(tfBit, bitOr(ifBit, bitOr(dfBit, ofBit)))
    yield bitOr(F002:u16, bitOr(arithmetic, controls))
  }
  flags "disable traps and mask INTR" simultaneously {
    TF := 0:flag
    IF := 0:flag
  } // Preserve unlisted flags.
  write recognitionDeferred:boolean := false
  write interruptDeferred:boolean := false
  write waiting:boolean := false
  write halted:boolean := false
  perform "push a captured word" {
    word:u16 := savedFlags
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0002:u16)
    segment:u16 := read SS
    offset:u16 := read SP
    perform "write a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
      pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
      contents:u16 := word
      segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
      offset := low16(pointer)
      write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)] := lowByte(contents)
      write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)] := highByte(contents)
    }
  }
  savedCS:u16 := read CS
  perform "push a captured word" {
    word:u16 := savedCS
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0002:u16)
    segment:u16 := read SS
    offset:u16 := read SP
    perform "write a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
      pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
      contents:u16 := word
      segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
      offset := low16(pointer)
      write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)] := lowByte(contents)
      write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)] := highByte(contents)
    }
  }
  savedIP:u16 := read IP
  perform "push a captured word" {
    word:u16 := savedIP
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0002:u16)
    segment:u16 := read SS
    offset:u16 := read SP
    perform "write a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
      pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
      contents:u16 := word
      segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
      offset := low16(pointer)
      write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)] := lowByte(contents)
      write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)] := highByte(contents)
    }
  }
  write CS:u16 := targetCS
  write IP:u16 := targetIP
}
```

```text
    offset := shiftBitsLeft(zeroExtend16(vector), 2)
    targetIP:u16 := source "read a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
      pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(0000:u16, offset)
      segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
      offset := low16(pointer)
      low:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)]
      high:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)]
      yield concatHighLow(high, low)
    }
    targetCS:u16 := source "read a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
      pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(0000:u16, addWrap(offset, 0002:u16))
      segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
      offset := low16(pointer)
      low:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)]
      high:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)]
      yield concatHighLow(high, low)
    }
    savedFlags:u16 := source "packed FLAGS word" {
      cf:flag := read CF
      pf:flag := read PF
      af:flag := read AF
      zf:flag := read ZF
      sf:flag := read SF
      tf:flag := read TF
      if:flag := read IF
      df:flag := read DF
      of:flag := read OF
      cfBit := select(cf, 0001:u16, 0000:u16)
      pfBit := select(pf, 0004:u16, 0000:u16)
      afBit := select(af, 0010:u16, 0000:u16)
      zfBit := select(zf, 0040:u16, 0000:u16)
      sfBit := select(sf, 0080:u16, 0000:u16)
      tfBit := select(tf, 0100:u16, 0000:u16)
      ifBit := select(if, 0200:u16, 0000:u16)
      dfBit := select(df, 0400:u16, 0000:u16)
      ofBit := select(of, 0800:u16, 0000:u16)
      arithmetic := bitOr(cfBit, bitOr(pfBit, bitOr(afBit, bitOr(zfBit, sfBit))))
      controls := bitOr(tfBit, bitOr(ifBit, bitOr(dfBit, ofBit)))
      yield bitOr(F002:u16, bitOr(arithmetic, controls))
    }
    flags "disable traps and mask INTR" simultaneously {
      TF := 0:flag
      IF := 0:flag
    } // Preserve unlisted flags.
    write recognitionDeferred:boolean := false
    write interruptDeferred:boolean := false
    write waiting:boolean := false
    write halted:boolean := false
    perform "push a captured word" {
      word:u16 := savedFlags
      pointer:u16 := read SP
      write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0002:u16)
      segment:u16 := read SS
      offset:u16 := read SP
      perform "write a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
        pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
        contents:u16 := word
        segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
        offset := low16(pointer)
        write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)] := lowByte(contents)
        write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)] := highByte(contents)
      }
    }
    savedCS:u16 := read CS
    perform "push a captured word" {
      word:u16 := savedCS
      pointer:u16 := read SP
      write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0002:u16)
      segment:u16 := read SS
      offset:u16 := read SP
      perform "write a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
        pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
        contents:u16 := word
        segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
        offset := low16(pointer)
        write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)] := lowByte(contents)
        write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)] := highByte(contents)
      }
    }
    savedIP:u16 := read IP
    perform "push a captured word" {
      word:u16 := savedIP
      pointer:u16 := read SP
      write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0002:u16)
      segment:u16 := read SS
      offset:u16 := read SP
      perform "write a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
        pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
        contents:u16 := word
        segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
        offset := low16(pointer)
        write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)] := lowByte(contents)
        write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)] := highByte(contents)
      }
    }
    write CS:u16 := targetCS
    write IP:u16 := targetIP
  }
  report completed software interrupt delivery, vector 04:u8
}
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, DF, OF.

### 8088 IRET

The formal entry action clears TF then IF and the recognition/wait/halt latches. It pushes FLAGS, live CS, and live IP, then commits target CS and IP after the complete frame succeeds. Software forms use `1100 11 tt`: INT3 (`tt=00`), INT with a fetched type byte (`01`), INTO (`10`), and IRET (`11`). `report interrupt` records completed software delivery; it performs no vector or stack effects itself.

```text
perform "return to a saved CS:IP" {
  discard:u16 := 0000:u16
  targetIP:u16 := source "pop segmented word" {
    segment:u16 := read SS
    offset:u16 := read SP
    word:u16 := source "read a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
      pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
      segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
      offset := low16(pointer)
      low:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)]
      high:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)]
      yield concatHighLow(high, low)
    }
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := addWrap(pointer, 0002:u16)
    yield word
  }
  targetCS:u16 := source "pop segmented word" {
    segment:u16 := read SS
    offset:u16 := read SP
    word:u16 := source "read a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
      pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
      segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
      offset := low16(pointer)
      low:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)]
      high:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)]
      yield concatHighLow(high, low)
    }
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := addWrap(pointer, 0002:u16)
    yield word
  }
  write IP:u16 := targetIP
  write CS:u16 := targetCS
  pointer:u16 := read SP
  write SP:u16 := addWrap(pointer, discard)
}
perform "restore stacked FLAGS with recognition delay" {
  status:u16 := source "pop segmented word" {
    segment:u16 := read SS
    offset:u16 := read SP
    word:u16 := source "read a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
      pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
      segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
      offset := low16(pointer)
      low:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)]
      high:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)]
      yield concatHighLow(high, low)
    }
    pointer:u16 := read SP
    write SP:u16 := addWrap(pointer, 0002:u16)
    yield word
  }
  oldIF:flag := read IF
  when not(oldIF) {
    when not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0200:u16))) {
      request INTR deferral at successful retirement
    }
  }
  perform "replace all FLAGS" {
    status:u16 := status
    replace flags "restore FLAGS" simultaneously {
      CF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0001:u16)))
      PF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0004:u16)))
      AF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0010:u16)))
      ZF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0040:u16)))
      SF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0080:u16)))
      TF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0100:u16)))
      IF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0200:u16)))
      DF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0400:u16)))
      OF := not(isZero(bitAnd(status, 0800:u16)))
    } // Replace the complete flag object.
  }
}
```

Flags preserved throughout: none.

### 8088 AAM

AAM/AAD (`1101 010 d`) require the documented `$0A` radix before accessing AX. AAM splits AL into quotient and remainder; AAD combines AH × 10 + AL and clears AH. After writing AX, both reread AL for ZF/SF/PF. CBW and CWD (`1001 100 s`) extend AL's sign to AX or AX's sign to DX without flag effects.

```text
radix:u8 := fetch byte
when not(isZero(subtract(radix, 0A:u8))) {
  return outcome "opcode"; no later effects
}
low:u8 := source "low byte of AX" {
  word:u16 := read AX
  yield lowByte(word)
}
quotient, remainder := divideUnsigned(zeroExtend16(low), 0A:u8)
// Truncate quotient toward zero; remainder follows dividend sign. Both results have divisor width.
// Zero divisor or quotient overflow returns "divide-error" before any later effect.
write AX:u16 := concatHighLow(quotient, remainder)
result:u8 := source "low byte of AX" {
  word:u16 := read AX
  yield lowByte(word)
}
flags "zero, sign, and parity" simultaneously {
  ZF := isZero(result)
  SF := topBit(result)
  PF := evenParity8(result)
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, AF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 LOOPNE rel8

LOOPNE/LOOPE/LOOP/JCXZ use `1110 00 cc`. LOOP decrements CX without changing flags, then rereads live CX. A zero count skips any ZF read; otherwise LOOPNE requires ZF clear and LOOPE requires it set. JCXZ tests CX once and never decrements it. Relative JMP uses `1110 10 s 1`, where `s=0` takes a word and `s=1` sign-extends a byte. All offsets are fetched before these effects.

```text
offset:u8 := source "immediate byte" {
  byte:u8 := fetch byte
  yield byte
}
counter:u16 := read CX
write CX:u16 := subtract(counter, 0001:u16)
remaining:u16 := read CX
when not(isZero(remaining)) {
  equal:flag := read ZF
  when not(equal) {
    perform "branch from live post-fetch IP" {
      offset:u16 := signExtend16(offset)
      position:u16 := read IP
      write IP:u16 := addWrap(position, offset)
    }
  }
}
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 CALL rel16

Near relative CALL (`1110 1000`) fetches its displacement, captures and pushes return IP, then adds the displacement to **live IP after both writes**. Immediate far CALL (`1001 1010`) fetches the complete offset and segment before pushing CS and then live IP. Far JMP (`1110 1010`) fetches the same pointer and writes CS before IP without a stack access. The far-transfer action also serves the indirect FF forms, after they have read their complete memory pointer.

```text

  low:u8 := fetch byte
  high:u8 := fetch byte
  yield concatHighLow(high, low)
}
returnIP:u16 := read IP
perform "push a captured word" {
  word:u16 := returnIP
  pointer:u16 := read SP
  write SP:u16 := subtract(pointer, 0002:u16)
  segment:u16 := read SS
  offset:u16 := read SP
  perform "write a captured 16-bit memory operand" {
    pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
    contents:u16 := word
    segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
    offset := low16(pointer)
    write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)] := lowByte(contents)
    write memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + addWrap(offset, 0001:u16), 20 bits)] := highByte(contents)
  }
}
perform "branch from live post-fetch IP" {
  offset:u16 := displacement
  position:u16 := read IP
  write IP:u16 := addWrap(position, offset)
}
```

### 8088 HLT

HLT sets the stored stopped latch; the boundary still owns retirement and pending traps. CMC complements live CF. CLC/STC and CLD/STD set their selected flag without reading it. CLI clears IF directly; STI reads IF, requests INTR deferral only when it was clear, then sets it. None of these bodies commits recognition latches itself. These requests remain explicit instruction effects.

```text
write halted:boolean := true
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 CLD

HLT sets the stored stopped latch; the boundary still owns retirement and pending traps. CMC complements live CF. CLC/STC and CLD/STD set their selected flag without reading it. CLI clears IF directly; STI reads IF, requests INTR deferral only when it was clear, then sets it. None of these bodies commits recognition latches itself. These requests remain explicit instruction effects.

```text
flags "set direction" simultaneously {
  DF := 0:flag
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, OF.

### 8088 STD

HLT sets the stored stopped latch; the boundary still owns retirement and pending traps. CMC complements live CF. CLC/STC and CLD/STD set their selected flag without reading it. CLI clears IF directly; STI reads IF, requests INTR deferral only when it was clear, then sets it. None of these bodies commits recognition latches itself. These requests remain explicit instruction effects.

```text
flags "set direction" simultaneously {
  DF := 1:flag
} // Preserve unlisted flags.
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, OF.

### 8088 ADD 8-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 ADD 16-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 ADD 8-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 ADD 16-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 OR 8-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 OR 16-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 OR 8-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 OR 16-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 ADC 8-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 ADC 16-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 ADC 8-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 ADC 16-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 SBB 8-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 SBB 16-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 SBB 8-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 SBB 16-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 AND 8-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 AND 16-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 AND 8-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 AND 16-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 SUB 8-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 SUB 16-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 SUB 8-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 SUB 16-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 XOR 8-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

### 8088 XOR 16-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 XOR 8-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 XOR 16-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 CMP 8-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 CMP 16-bit r/m,r

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 CMP 8-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 CMP 16-bit r,r/m

`00 ooo 0 d w` selects the same eight operations as the accumulator-immediate encodings. Resolve ModR/M first, capture the source selected by `d`, then read the destination and any incoming CF. Failed resolution or operand reads prevent later flags and writeback; completed effects remain visible on failure.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 ALU 8-bit r/m,n ($80)

Capture the pointer, fetch the complete immediate, then read the destination and any incoming CF. This sequence keeps displacement and immediate callbacks from retargeting the memory operand. CMP updates flags without writeback.

### 8088 ALU 16-bit r/m,n ($81)

### 8088 ALU 8-bit r/m,n ($82)

### 8088 ALU 16-bit r/m,signed byte ($83)

Capture the pointer, fetch the complete immediate, then read the destination and any incoming CF. This sequence keeps displacement and immediate callbacks from retargeting the memory operand. CMP updates flags without writeback.

### 8088 TEST 8-bit r/m,r

### 8088 XCHG 8-bit r/m,r

`1000 011 w` selects XCHG r/m,r. Resolve the pointer first, then capture r/m before the `ggg` register. Write them in that order from the captured originals, retaining completed writes if a later effect fails. Preserve all flags.

### 8088 MOV 8-bit r/m,r

`1000 10 d w` is MOV r/m,r or r,r/m. Fetch ModR/M and resolve its memory operand before reading either value. `d=0` selects r/m as destination; `d=1` selects the `ggg` register. `w=0/1` selects byte/word operands. Preserve flags; a failed address or source read prevents writeback.

### 8088 MOV 16-bit r/m,r

`1000 10 d w` is MOV r/m,r or r,r/m. Fetch ModR/M and resolve its memory operand before reading either value. `d=0` selects r/m as destination; `d=1` selects the `ggg` register. `w=0/1` selects byte/word operands. Preserve flags; a failed address or source read prevents writeback.

### 8088 MOV 8-bit r,r/m

`1000 10 d w` is MOV r/m,r or r,r/m. Fetch ModR/M and resolve its memory operand before reading either value. `d=0` selects r/m as destination; `d=1` selects the `ggg` register. `w=0/1` selects byte/word operands. Preserve flags; a failed address or source read prevents writeback.

### 8088 MOV 16-bit r,r/m

`1000 10 d w` is MOV r/m,r or r,r/m. Fetch ModR/M and resolve its memory operand before reading either value. `d=0` selects r/m as destination; `d=1` selects the `ggg` register. `w=0/1` selects byte/word operands. Preserve flags; a failed address or source read prevents writeback.

### 8088 MOV r/m16,Sreg

MOV segment forms use `1000 11 d 0` and ModR/M `mm 0ss rrr`: `d=0` stores a segment and `d=1` loads one. Reject invalid segment selectors, including a CS destination, before resolving the address. Capture a complete source before the write; only a successful segment load requests recognition deferral. Each memory word uses the captured pointer and low-first accesses.

### 8088 LEA r16,m

LEA (`1000 1101`) resolves a memory address and writes its sixteen-bit offset without reading data. LES/LDS (`1100 010 s`) read offset then segment from memory, low byte first, before writing the selected general register and then ES/DS. Neither far load requests interrupt inhibition. All three reject `mm=11` before resolving or reading an operand. XLAT (`1101 0111`) reads BX then AL, wraps their sum, then selects DS or the captured override; it reads one byte and writes AL while preserving live AH.

### 8088 MOV Sreg,r/m16

MOV segment forms use `1000 11 d 0` and ModR/M `mm 0ss rrr`: `d=0` stores a segment and `d=1` loads one. Reject invalid segment selectors, including a CS destination, before resolving the address. Capture a complete source before the write; only a successful segment load requests recognition deferral. Each memory word uses the captured pointer and low-first accesses.

### 8088 POP r/m16

`0101 p rrr` selects register PUSH/POP. Original 8088 PUSH SP differs from other registers: its source is the captured SP minus two, before the stack's independent pointer update. The separate source makes that exception visible; all other encoded registers use the ordinary register catalogue.

### 8088 MOV AL,[offset]

`1010 00 d w` moves between the accumulator and an absolute offset. Fetch the whole offset first. Read DS only if no segment override was captured, then use the same resolved transfer actions. `d=0` loads AL/AX; `d=1` stores it. Do not read a memory destination or change flags.

### 8088 LES r16,m

LES/LDS (`1100 010 s`) read offset then segment from memory, low byte first, before writing the selected general register and then ES/DS. Neither far load requests interrupt inhibition. XLAT (`1101 0111`) reads BX then AL, wraps their sum, then selects DS or the captured override; it reads one byte and writes AL while preserving live AH.

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 LDS r16,m

LEA (`1000 1101`) resolves a memory address and writes its sixteen-bit offset without reading data. LES/LDS (`1100 010 s`) read offset then segment from memory, low byte first, before writing the selected general register and then ES/DS. Neither far load requests interrupt inhibition. All three reject `mm=11` before resolving or reading an operand. XLAT (`1101 0111`) reads BX then AL, wraps their sum, then selects DS or the captured override; it reads one byte and writes AL while preserving live AH.

### 8088 MOV 8-bit r/m,n

`1100 011 w` permits only ModR/M `/0` for immediate MOV. Reject every other operation selector before displacement or immediate fetches. Resolve any memory destination, fetch the complete immediate, then write once without reading the destination. Byte-register writes preserve the live other half.

### 8088 MOV 16-bit r/m,n

`1100 011 w` permits only ModR/M `/0` for immediate MOV. Reject every other operation selector before displacement or immediate fetches. Resolve any memory destination, fetch the complete immediate, then write once without reading the destination. Byte-register writes preserve the live other half.

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 8-bit shifts/rotates by one

Memory forms fetch the complete encoding, read the operand once, perform all movements internally, then write it once. A zero count also records a read and unchanged write. Word accesses retain the segment-offset wrapping policy. These are explicit instruction-level access rules, without cycle counts or prefetch effects. The chapter describes each movement and its ordered flag updates.

### 8088 16-bit shifts/rotates by one

Memory forms fetch the complete encoding, read the operand once, perform all movements internally, then write it once. A zero count also records a read and unchanged write. Word accesses retain the segment-offset wrapping policy. These are explicit instruction-level access rules, without cycle counts or prefetch effects. The chapter describes each movement and its ordered flag updates.

### 8088 8-bit shifts/rotates by CL

Memory forms fetch the complete encoding, read the operand once, perform all movements internally, then write it once. A zero count also records a read and unchanged write. Word accesses retain the segment-offset wrapping policy. These are explicit instruction-level access rules, without cycle counts or prefetch effects. The chapter describes each movement and its ordered flag updates.

Flags preserved throughout: TF, IF, DF.

### 8088 16-bit shifts/rotates by CL

Memory forms fetch the complete encoding, read the operand once, perform all movements internally, then write it once. A zero count also records a read and unchanged write. Word accesses retain the segment-offset wrapping policy. These are explicit instruction-level access rules, without cycle counts or prefetch effects. The chapter describes each movement and its ordered flag updates.

### 8088 XLAT

LEA (`1000 1101`) resolves a memory address and writes its sixteen-bit offset without reading data. LES/LDS (`1100 010 s`) read offset then segment from memory, low byte first, before writing the selected general register and then ES/DS. Neither far load requests interrupt inhibition. All three reject `mm=11` before resolving or reading an operand. XLAT (`1101 0111`) reads BX then AL, wraps their sum, then selects DS or the captured override; it reads one byte and writes AL while preserving live AH.

```text
overridden:u8 := input
segmentOverride:u16 := input
base:u16 := read BX
index:u8 := source "low byte of AX" {
  word:u16 := read AX
  yield lowByte(word)
}
offset := addWrap(base, zeroExtend16(index))
segment:u16 := source "DS unless a segment override was captured" {
  overridden:u8 := overridden
  segmentOverride:u16 := segmentOverride
  segment:u16 := match byte overridden {
    case (byte & FF) = 00 {
      original:u16 := read DS
      yield original
    }
    case (byte & FF) = 01 {
      yield segmentOverride
    }
    otherwise return outcome "unsupported"; no later effects
  }
  yield segment
}
contents:u8 := source "read a captured 8-bit memory operand" {
  pointer:u32 := concatHighLow(segment, offset)
  segment := low16(shiftBitsRight(pointer, 16))
  offset := low16(pointer)
  low:u8 := read memory[projectAddress(segment * 16 + offset, 20 bits)]
  yield low
}
perform "write AL, preserving its other half" {
  byte:u8 := contents
  preservedWord:u16 := read AX
  write AX:u16 := concatHighLow(highByte(preservedWord), byte)
}
```

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 ESC 0

ESC uses `1101 1 ooo` and ModR/M `mm ppp rrr`; `ooo:ppp` forms the six-bit coprocessor opcode. Register forms send the selector without reading CPU registers. Memory forms resolve the ordinary segmented address and read a complete dummy word even if no coprocessor is connected. Only then do they send the captured segment, offset, physical address, and word. The device adapter detaches requests and records only successful delivery. ESC itself leaves CPU state and flags unchanged; no coprocessor arithmetic is emulated.

Flags preserved throughout: CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF.

### 8088 ESC 1

ESC uses `1101 1 ooo` and ModR/M `mm ppp rrr`; `ooo:ppp` forms the six-bit coprocessor opcode. Register forms send the selector without reading CPU registers. Memory forms resolve the ordinary segmented address and read a complete dummy word even if no coprocessor is connected. Only then do they send the captured segment, offset, physical address, and word. The device adapter detaches requests and records only successful delivery. ESC itself leaves CPU state and flags unchanged; no coprocessor arithmetic is emulated.
